headline: Recommended adoption of ADU zoning amendments and elected George Gomes as Planning Board Chair.
summary: The board recessed for a public hearing on proposed amendments to the Beverly Zoning Ordinance on Accessory Dwelling Units, which align local rules with the Acts of 2024. After discussion and no public comment, the board voted to recommend adoption of the amendments. The board also elected George Gomes as Chair, tabled the Vice Chair vote until July 2026, and approved the April 28, 2026 minutes as amended.
decisions: Closed the Public Hearing on the proposed ADU amendments, 6-0.
Recommended adoption of the proposed ADU amendments, 6-0.
Amended motion to recommend adoption of the proposed ADU amendments, noting the State is aligning with Beverly's ADU rules, carried 6-0.
Elected George Gomes as Chair of the Beverly Planning Board, 5-0-1 (Gomes abstaining).
Tabled the vote for Vice Chair until July 2026, 6-0.
Approved the April 28, 2026 meeting minutes, as amended, 6-0.

Clawson reviewed the proposed updates which are to change the language so that it is in concert 32 
with the Acts of 2024. The Acts of 2024 trump the Ordinance. This helps to align the Ordinance 33 
with the State law so that there is less confusion. This will also eliminate confusion between the 34 
State’s protected accessory dwelling unit (ADU) laws and the local laws. Beckwith noted that 35

ADU created in the past year under the Ordinance are considered local use ADUs. Someone with 37 
a local use ADU is still allowed to build a protected use ADU. If the local use ADU had any 38 
provisions on it, such as it being used by a family member or requiring a parking space, those 39 
requirements have to remain to keep the local use ADU active. The less restrictive use is 40 
grandfathered in. The protected use ADU allows for 1,000 s.f. or half the gross floor area of the 41 
principal structure. The State allows for 900 s.f., but the local ordinance allows for 1,000 s.f. 42 
which is allowed to be used, as it is less restrictive. Also, if a zone allows a single-family 43 
residential house, an ADU unit is allowed. Owner occupancy is also no longer required. ADUs 44 
cannot be used for short-term rentals, as the City does not allow them. Another change is that the 45
